paragraphs: (He was expert in plene and defective spellings.) He is mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim, chapter 3, beginning of halakhah 1; in Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat, chapter 9, halakhah 2, he is called Rabbi Chuna.[^1][^2]

notes.text: ספרא דסדרא is retained as Safra deSidra rather than assigning “Order” as an established institutional title. The Guggenheimer digital text of Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 3:1 fully writes Rav Huna Safra deSidra in the discussion of plene spellings, supporting that contextual wording. Hyman’s separate Shabbat 9:2 Chuna form is preserved.

The consulted Guggenheimer Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 3:1 paragraph names Rav Huna Safra deSidra in the discussion of plene spellings. Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 9:2 names Rabbi Chuna Safra deSidra in the corresponding discussion. These support the local title distinction and Hyman’s spelling explanation, without establishing a historical identity between the two references or assigning a new institutional meaning to deSidra.
